meta.defaultDescription: CIIM is the Molecular Engineering Research Center at Universidad Católica de Santa María (Arequipa, Peru). Molecular dynamics, bioinformatics, chem-informatics, drug discovery, meta-analysis and QM/MM.

footer.tagline: The Molecular Engineering Research Center (CIIM) at Universidad Católica de Santa María drives computational research advancing molecular biology.

hero.subtitle: CIIM at Universidad Católica de Santa María drives molecular engineering research using computational methods, training researchers to advance the life sciences.

research.title: Advancing Scientific Knowledge
research.description: Our research center combines computational methods, molecular analysis, and data science to push the boundaries of scientific discovery and innovation.

researchPage.title: Research – CIIM
researchPage.description: CIIM research areas: molecular dynamics, bioinformatics, chem-informatics, drug discovery, meta-analysis and QM/MM applied to molecular engineering.
researchPage.heroSubtitle: Explore the research areas of our center, where computational methods are applied to fundamental problems in molecular biology.

researchAreas.title: Molecular Dynamics
researchAreas.description: Simulate the physical movements of atoms and molecules over time to gain insights into structural stability, conformational changes, and thermodynamic properties of biomolecular systems.

researchAreas.title: Bioinformatics
researchAreas.description: Analyze and interpret biological data using computational tools and algorithms, enabling discoveries in genomics, transcriptomics, and personalized medicine.

researchAreas.title: Chem-Informatics
researchAreas.description: Utilize chemical structure data and informatics techniques to discover patterns, predict properties, and guide rational drug design and compound optimization.

researchAreas.title: Drug Discovery
researchAreas.description: Accelerate the identification and optimization of potential therapeutic compounds using integrated computational pipelines, screening libraries, and predictive models.

researchAreas.title: Meta-Analysis
researchAreas.description: Integrate and statistically analyze results from multiple studies to derive robust, evidence-based conclusions across large biological datasets or clinical trials.

researchAreas.title: QM/MM
researchAreas.description: Combine quantum mechanics and molecular mechanics methods to study chemical and biological phenomena with high accuracy, especially at reaction sites and enzymatic systems.

ifmsaPage.title: IFMSA Exchange Projects – CIIM
ifmsaPage.description: CIIM research projects available through the IFMSA exchange program for medical students: proteins, biopharmaceuticals and molecular interactions.
ifmsaPage.heroSubtitle: Explore international medical exchange opportunities and shape your future in global healthcare.

ifmsaProjects.name: Mutations in SHP2 Protein (PTPN11) & LEOPARD Syndrome
ifmsaProjects.description: Analyze structural effects of PTPN11 mutations causing LEOPARD Syndrome using molecular dynamics and Ramachandran validation.
features: Model selection from PDB & homology modeling
System setup: solvation, ions, minimization & equilibration

ifmsaProjects.name: Phytoestrogens from Aguaje vs. COVID-19 Spike Protein
ifmsaProjects.description: Evaluate complexation of Mauritia flexuosa phytoestrogens with SARS-CoV-2 spike protein via docking and MD simulations.
features: Force field parametrization & quantum charge calculations
MD setup: solvation, ions, minimization & equilibration

ifmsaProjects.name: GLP-1 Receptor & Analog Interaction Properties
ifmsaProjects.description: Investigate physicochemical and thermodynamic interactions between GLP-1 receptor and its pharmaceutical analogs via simulations.
features: PDB model retrieval & missing region building
System preparation: solvation, ions, minimization & equilibration

publicationsPage.title: Publications – CIIM
publicationsPage.description: Scientific publications of CIIM in indexed journals (MDPI): anticonvulsant macamides, PARP-1 inhibitors, tuberculosis, bacterial resistance and nanoparticles.
publicationsPage.heroSubtitle: Discover the scientific publications of our center in indexed international journals.

publications.title: Anticonvulsant Effects of Synthetic N-(3-Methoxybenzyl)oleamide and N-(3-Methoxybenzyl)linoleamide Macamides: An In Silico and In Vivo Study
publications.description: This study evaluates the anticonvulsant properties of novel synthetic macamides through computational and animal model analyses, indicating their potential therapeutic applications.
publications.author: PhD. Badhin Gómez Valdez

publications.title: A Theoretical Study on the Efficacy and Mechanism of Combined YAP-1 and PARP-1 Inhibitors in the Treatment of Glioblastoma Multiforme Using Peruvian Maca Lepidium meyenii
publications.description: This theoretical research explores the combined use of YAP-1 and PARP-1 inhibitors derived from Peruvian Maca in treating glioblastoma multiforme, suggesting enhanced therapeutic efficacy.
publications.author: PhD. Badhin Gómez Valdez

publications.title: A Theoretical Study of the Interaction of PARP-1 with Natural and Synthetic Inhibitors: Advances in the Therapy of Triple-Negative Breast Cancer
publications.description: This study investigates the interactions between PARP-1 and various inhibitors, providing insights into potential advancements in treating triple-negative breast cancer.
publications.author: PhD. Badhin Gómez Valdez

publications.title: Study of the Rv1417 and Rv2617c Membrane Proteins and Their Interactions with Nicotine Derivatives as Potential Inhibitors of Erp Virulence-Associated Factor in Mycobacterium tuberculosis: An In Silico Approach
publications.description: This in silico study analyzes the interactions between specific membrane proteins and nicotine derivatives, aiming to identify potential inhibitors of virulence factors in Mycobacterium tuberculosis.
publications.author: PhD. Badhin Gómez Valdez

publications.title: Theoretical Study at the Molecular Mechanics Level of the Interaction of Tetracycline and Chloramphenicol with the Antibiotic Receptors Present in Enterococcus faecalis (Q839F7) and Streptococcus mutans (Q8DS20)
publications.description: This theoretical study examines how tetracycline and chloramphenicol interact with specific antibiotic receptors, providing insights into bacterial resistance mechanisms.
publications.author: PhD. Badhin Gómez Valdez

publications.title: Design and Evaluation of Polymer-Based Nanoparticles for Targeted Drug Delivery in Cancer Therapy
publications.description: This research focuses on designing polymer-based nanoparticles to enhance targeted drug delivery in cancer therapy, aiming to improve treatment efficacy and reduce side effects.
publications.author: PhD. Badhin Gómez Valdez
